reason: The paper states the three LDS grades (this being the Ni-free Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C / 28Mn0Ni grade) were prepared by vacuum induction melting to produce 30 kg ingots; this is the casting stage of the as-cast plus homogenised sample.

Explicit statement that the defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours, and that Fig. 1(a,b) presents the as-cast plus homogenised condition of 28Mn0Ni - this defines the sample's process.

The only microstructural description pertaining to the as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni condition is given in section 3.1 and Fig. 1(a); the grain-size / phase-fraction / twin-fraction values reported in Table 2 are for the hot-rolled condition and are therefore not attributed to this sample.
Overall as-cast plus homogenised microstructure of the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy taken from the text and the Fig. 1(a) description.

Fig. 1(a) (as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni) is described as equiaxed austenite grains, and the text states the 28Mn0Ni alloy in the as-cast plus homogenised condition is primarily made of a single phase, whereas the Ni-containing alloys are two-phase.
Fig. 1(a) optical micrograph of the as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni is described as equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles.

Optical microscopy was performed with an Olympus optical microscope (section 2.3), and Fig. 1(a)/(b) present the as-cast plus homogenised and hot-rolled micrographs of 28Mn0Ni - panel (a) belongs to the as-homogenised sample.
